entries.verbatim:
Taking this up involves several concrete acts and exposures. It commits you to a low-pressure one-to-one with the avoiding friend before calling any group meeting, and to listening there without rebutting; raising it as an ambush about chores would confirm whatever made the conversations feel bad in the first place. It commits you to proposing a written, specific agreement format and to accepting the small ongoing overhead of maintaining it, with the stated risk that the upkeep itself becomes a new chore and quite possibly yours. It commits you to a weekly reallocation in which you will sometimes accept the worse share, and to stating and negotiating your own minimum cleanliness standard rather than treating it as obvious.

The advice depends on the assumption that the disputes are mainly ambiguity-and-logistics problems. If the friend's withdrawal reflects a deeper grievance, such as a long-standing sense that effort is uneven or that the deck is stacked, a process fix alone will not hold; the one-to-one is partly a test of which situation you are in.

Open criticism to keep in view: the written record can be attacked as bureaucratic or as a device for winning arguments rather than ending them. Its defence is that it targets exactly the failure you reported, namely disagreement about what was agreed; deployed pointedly or triumphantly it will instead deepen the avoidance.

Unresolved: whether the friend will re-engage at all; whether three different standards can actually be reconciled; and how any system survives a genuinely chaotic week, which is when it will first be tested.

entries.verbatim: Taking up this account commits one to the following. Central conjecture, not established fact: that the recurring 'what did the agreement mean' disputes arise largely from underspecified, unrecorded agreements rather than bad faith — the material cannot distinguish this from a masked fairness grievance, so both readings stay open and the first review conversation is committed to probing for a real imbalance rather than assuming there is none. Proposed application: explicit, small, written, time-limited arrangements, with confirmation messages after agreements and a standing review point; this is offered as low-cost and reversible, testable only in the trying, with no guarantee attached. Interpretive claim offered at low confidence: that the avoiding friend's behaviour is both symptom and cause of the failing process; alternatives (feeling ganged-up on, disengaging from the friendship) would call for a different response, so the proposed one-to-one functions partly as a diagnostic rather than a remedy. Distinction relied on: ambiguity problem versus willingness problem versus fairness problem — treated as separable and possibly coexisting. Scope limit: the advice is addressed to one of three flatmates who cannot compel the others; if the others refuse any engagement, these proposals mostly lapse and the problem shifts to a different one (the viability of the living arrangement), which this account does not address. Methodological constraint honoured: no facts were invented beyond the material given; everything beyond it is marked as conjecture. Nothing here commits anyone to escalation, mediation, or moving out — and nothing rules those out either.

entries.verbatim: Taking up this objection involves the following. A proposed revision to the instrument, not a ban on it: any written arrangement should be jointly authored at the moment of agreement, and confirmation messages should come from the non-drafting party or be co-written, since the criticism depends on treating the record as contested ground rather than neutral record-keeping — and this revision itself concedes the original proposal may work fine in households where the ambiguity reading is correct. A weakened claim the critic is committed to defending or dropping: the intervention-as-bet point stands only if no discriminating observation was specified; if 'disputes recur over recorded items' or similar is read back into the source account, that ground of objection lapses. A dependence to flag: the criticism leans on a rival hypothesis — motivated reinterpretation, and avoidance possibly directed at the asker — which is asserted as at least as consistent with the single-source material as the ambiguity reading, not established; evidence that disputes persist despite clear written terms would defeat the rival and blunt most of this objection. An unresolved problem the objection names but does not solve: what the asker should do if the avoider will not engage at all remains open — neither the account nor this criticism addresses the collapsed-engagement case beyond identifying it as the probable hard case. What is retained from the source account: expiry-and-review and the explicit surfacing of possible imbalance are taken up as sound and independent of the criticised conjecture. No commitment is made here to escalation, mediation, or to treating the asker's report as unreliable — the single-source caveat is a methodological caution, not an accusation — and if the objection, its relevance, or its reading of the problem is mistaken, the pieces to salvage first are the jointly-authored-record revision and the demand for a discriminating observation.
